headline: Chip-factory prices jump 12.9% as Europe's power bills climb again
text:
# Chip-factory prices jump 12.9% as Europe's power bills climb again

The day's numbers point one way: prices for electronics and household electricity are rising fast, while coal, Estonian car sales and Egyptian FDI show how quickly a level can vanish.

## Today in the data

### US electronics prices break their range
[US factory-gate prices: computers and electronics vs machinery (yoy %)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Computer and electronic producer prices rose 12.9% in the year to Aug 2026 (index 120.0; us-ppi-sectors), against a usual +0.6%. Machinery (+3.9%) and electrical equipment (+4.4%) are firm but nowhere near it, so the move is sector-specific rather than general — worth checking against the us-chips series. Base periods differ across these indices, so read growth rates only.

### Austria's power bill at a record
[Household electricity, all taxes: Austria and Luxembourg, EUR/kWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian households paid EUR 0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on a year earlier and the largest rise since 2008 (energy-household-eu). Luxembourg did the same thing, +31.7% to 0.2665. Note the base: Austria's H2 2024 reading of 0.2437 was itself a dip from 0.2731, so relief measures dropping out of the price inflate the change.

### Austrian pharma output halves
[Austrian pharma output against all manufacturing, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian pharma production was 160.4 (2021=100) in Jul 2026, down 45.7% on the year, the sharpest fall since the series starts in 2011 (eu-ipi-sectors). Total manufacturing sat at 102.6, so this is one sector unwinding a 2025 spike, not an industrial recession. Pharma volume indices are notoriously spiky in small countries and revise.

### UK coal all but gone
[UK electricity generation: coal, gas and wind, TWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% from 1.90 TWh in 2024 and the sharpest fall in a record beginning in 1921 (electricity-mix). Wind at 85.8 TWh is now close to gas at 90.9 TWh — the crossover is the thing to watch on the chart. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure.

### Estonian car market halves
[New car registrations in Estonia by fuel](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% from 25,744 in 2024; diesel fell 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). Battery-electric registrations were only 872, so the fall is the whole market shrinking rather than a switch of fuel. A registration-tax change would do this; the series is annual and short, from 2014 only.

### Egypt's FDI gives back a spike
[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Net FDI into Egypt was USD 15.45bn in 2025, USD 31.1bn below 2024's USD 46.58bn, the sharpest fall since 1971 (macro-external). The chart shows 2024 as a one-year tower above a decade near USD 10bn, so the fall is a return to trend. World Bank data lag one to two years and these figures revise.

### Hungarian mining output doubles
[Hungarian mining and quarrying output, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Hungarian mining and quarrying stood at 155.7 (2021=100) in Jul 2026, up 101.9% on the year, the biggest rise since Sep 2018 (eu-mining-ipi). The level has climbed from 125.2 in May to 155.7 in July, so this is a genuine run, not one odd month. Mining is a tiny share of Hungarian industry and the index swings hard.

## Forecasts

### Electronics prices keep grinding higher
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 120.048 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with period 12, fitting the 2010–2026 sample with a MAPE of 0.28% and residual standard deviation 0.42 index points. It projects 122.33 by Nov 2026, with a 95% band of 120.90 to 123.77. The band is only the spread of past one-step errors scaled up, not a statement about tariffs or chip supply. A single large monthly jump of the kind seen this summer, or a tariff schedule change, would put the outcome above it.

### Austrian pharma flat near 160
[eu-ipi-sectors:AT|C21: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 160.4 in Jul 2026 (eu-ipi-sectors). Holt-Winters additive, period 12, was chosen, but it fits far less well: MAPE 5.0% and residual standard deviation 12.1 index points. The Oct 2026 point forecast is 165.7 with a 95% band of 124.7 to 206.8 — a band that wide is an admission that this series jumps. It projects past behaviour only; another plant-level swing of the 2025 kind, or Eurostat's revisions, would take it outside.

## Correlations
- **US computer-electronic PPI vs electrical-equipment PPI** (yoy, 2010-01–2026-08, n=200): r = 0.567, lag −4 (electrical leads), clears the widened Bartlett band of 0.494. Input-cost pressure in electrical goods shows up in electronics prices about four months later, but the peak is the largest of 25 lags — treat it as a hypothesis.
- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, half-yearly 2008-S1–2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.531 contemporaneous. Moderate co-movement, consistent with shared wholesale and tax-relief timing; the levels correlation of 0.887 is just two trends and means nothing.

## What to watch
- **us-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): whether September extends the 12.9% electronics jump or reverses it.
- **eu-ipi-sectors** and **eu-mining-ipi** (both last 2026-07): August settles whether Austrian pharma has found a floor and Hungarian mining keeps doubling.
- **energy-household-eu**: the H1 2026 print shows whether Austria's 0.3272 is a new plateau.
- **eu-hicp** and **cpi-eu** (last 2026-07): the consumer side of the electricity rise.
- **eu-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): Europe's mirror of the US electronics move.

## Sources
- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-08.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes, EUR/kWh; last 2025-S2.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021=100, calendar adjusted; last 2026-07.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute, via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda; last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators; last 2025.
- eu-mining-ipi — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021=100; last 2026-07.
